title: Stalking
summary: Willfully and maliciously repeatedly following or harassing another person, plus a credible threat intended to put that person in reasonable fear for their own or immediate family safety. A credible threat requires apparent ability; actual intent to carry it out is not required. Constitutionally protected activity and labor picketing are excluded.
penalty: Ordinary wobbler: up to 364 days in county jail and/or a fine up to $1,000, or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison under section 18. Qualifying orders and prior convictions change the sentencing branch. Counseling is a probation condition unless excused for good cause; the court considers a protective order up to ten years. Court-ordered registration under 290.006 is possible for a felony, not automatic. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Willful, malicious conduct and specific intent to cause reasonable fear; the charged order/prior condition must also be established.

title: Stalking while a protective order is in effect
summary: Willfully and maliciously repeatedly following or harassing another person, plus a credible threat intended to put that person in reasonable fear for their own or immediate family safety. A credible threat requires apparent ability; actual intent to carry it out is not required. Constitutionally protected activity and labor picketing are excluded. A restraining order, injunction or other court order against the same party must prohibit the stalking behavior and be in effect.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3 or 4 years in state prison. The fine treatment requires review with the underlying 646.9(a) branch; no new fine ceiling is inferred. Counseling is a probation condition unless excused for good cause; the court considers a protective order up to ten years. Court-ordered registration under 290.006 is possible for a felony, not automatic. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Willful, malicious conduct and specific intent to cause reasonable fear; the charged order/prior condition must also be established.

A credible threat requires apparent ability; actual intent to carry it out is not required. Constitutionally protected activity and labor picketing are excluded. Requires a prior felony conviction under 273.5, 273.6 or 422, not merely any prior offense.
penalty: Wobbler: up to 364 days in county jail and/or a fine up to $1,000, or 2, 3 or 5 years in state prison. Counseling is a probation condition unless excused for good cause; the court considers a protective order up to ten years. Court-ordered registration under 290.006 is possible for a felony, not automatic. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.

Requires a prior felony conviction under 646.9(a).

title: Interfering with civil rights by force or threat
summary: Willfully using force or a threat of force to interfere with another person's legally protected rights, at least partly because of an actual or perceived protected characteristic under 422.55. Speech alone is insufficient unless it threatens violence against a specific person or group and the defendant has apparent ability to carry it out. When there are multiple motives, the prohibited bias must be a substantial factor; it need not be the only or main factor.
penalty: Wobbler under current 422.6(c): up to 364 days in county jail and/or a fine up to $5,000, or the 1170(h) default term of 16 months, 2 years or 3 years. The retained jury-instruction misdemeanor heading does not reflect this felony alternative. Community service is additionally required, capped at 400 hours over no more than 350 days, outside work/school hours; the statute does not state a numeric minimum. Custody under 1170(h) is ordinarily served in county jail, with statutory state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Willful interference or knowing property damage with the specified bias and interference purpose; protected expression is not itself an offense.

title: Interfering with civil rights by damaging property
summary: Knowingly defacing, damaging or destroying another person's property for the purpose of intimidating or interfering with legally protected rights, at least partly because of an actual or perceived protected characteristic under 422.55. When there are multiple motives, the prohibited bias must be a substantial factor; it need not be the only or main factor.
penalty: Wobbler under current 422.6(c): up to 364 days in county jail and/or a fine up to $5,000, or the 1170(h) default term of 16 months, 2 years or 3 years. The retained jury-instruction misdemeanor heading does not reflect this felony alternative. Community service is additionally required, capped at 400 hours over no more than 350 days, outside work/school hours; the statute does not state a numeric minimum. Custody under 1170(h) is ordinarily served in county jail, with statutory state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Willful interference or knowing property damage with the specified bias and interference purpose; protected expression is not itself an offense.

title: Hanging a noose to terrorize
summary: Hanging a noose on another person's private property without authorization, with purpose to terrorize its owner/occupant or reckless disregard of that risk; the separate listed-site alternative requires purpose to terrorize someone associated with the school, campus, public place, place of worship, cemetery or employment site. Knowledge that the noose represents a threat to life.
penalty: Wobbler. First conviction: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under 1170(h) and/or a fine up to $10,000, or up to 364 days in county jail and/or a fine up to $5,000. A second or subsequent conviction under (b), (c) or (d) retains the custody alternatives but raises the felony fine ceiling to $15,000 and misdemeanor ceiling to $10,000. Custody under 1170(h) is ordinarily served in county jail, with statutory state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: The specified knowledge and terrorizing purpose or private-property reckless-disregard alternative.

The provision concerns terrorizing conduct; peaceful Hindu, Buddhist and Jain swastika symbols are not criminalized merely as symbols.
penalty: Wobbler. First conviction: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under 1170(h) and/or a fine up to $10,000, or up to 364 days in county jail and/or a fine up to $5,000. A second or subsequent conviction under (b), (c) or (d) retains the custody alternatives but raises the felony fine ceiling to $15,000 and misdemeanor ceiling to $10,000. Custody under 1170(h) is ordinarily served in county jail, with statutory state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: The specified knowledge and terrorizing purpose or private-property reckless-disregard alternative.

A second or subsequent conviction under (b), (c) or (d) retains the custody alternatives but raises the felony fine ceiling to $15,000 and misdemeanor ceiling to $10,000. Custody under 1170(h) is ordinarily served in county jail, with statutory state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown. title: Interfering with religious exercise by a direct threat
summary: With intent to cause another to refrain from religious exercise or a religious service, causing or attempting to cause that result through a directly communicated threat of unlawful injury to a person or property. It must reasonably appear to the recipient that the threat can be carried out.
penalty: Felony: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison under section 18. A fine up to $10,000 may also be imposed under section 672. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Specific intent to interfere with religious exercise through the described credible threat.

title: Terrorizing by explosive device or arson at a specified place
summary: Exploding, igniting or attempting to explode or ignite a destructive device or explosive, or committing arson, in or about a place specifically listed in 11413(b), with purpose to terrorize another or reckless disregard of terrorizing another. The listed place or bias-targeted private-property condition must be proved; an ordinary property fire alone does not establish this offense.
penalty: Felony: 3, 5 or 7 years under 1170(h), and a fine up to $10,000. Custody under 1170(h) is ordinarily served in county jail, with statutory state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Purpose to terrorize or reckless disregard of terrorizing; the charged destructive-device, explosive or arson elements must be established.

title: Possession of a destructive device
summary: Knowingly possessing a destructive device within California, with knowledge of the device's defining characteristics. Fixed ammunition over .60 caliber is excluded from this section; chapter exceptions and permits must be considered.
penalty: Wobbler: up to 364 days in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison under section 18, a fine up to $10,000, or both fine and custody. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Knowing possession and knowledge of the characteristics making it a destructive device.

title: Possessing an explosive or destructive device at a specified place

The charged location and statutory device/explosive definition must be established.
penalty: Felony: 2, 4 or 6 years under 1170(h). A fine up to $10,000 may also be imposed under section 672. Custody under 1170(h) is ordinarily served in county jail, with statutory state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Reckless or malicious possession; knowledge of the item and its explosive/destructive character.

Custody under 1170(h) is ordinarily served in county jail, with statutory state-prison exclusions. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, firearm restrictions and case-specific sentencing require separate review.

penalty: Misdemeanor: three months to 364 days in county jail, unless a different penalty applies. A fine may also be imposed under section 672, up to $1,000 where no other fine is prescribed.
